TF212344.headline: A roll of track, not a box of track
overview: The TF212344 is a roll of blue PVC track with two lanes running side by side, supplied wound on itself with the black clamp stands packed separately. The track is flexible, so the child sets the height and the shape: the photographs show it looped into a vertical curve, run flat across a floor, and angled down from a table edge using the clamp stands, which are moulded with suction cups at the foot. Two small sports cars are included. Nothing about the layout is fixed, which is the difference between this and the moulded dinosaur track sets further up this collection: those build one shape, this one can be rebuilt in a minute and stored as a roll.

The packing is the most efficient in the track range. A carton holds 16 pieces at 0.077 CBM and 20 kg gross, so 1.25 kg per unit and 363 cartons on a 20GP, 5,808 pieces. The 80-piece minimum is five cartons and 0.385 CBM. Because the product is a rolled strip rather than a rigid assembled layout, the retail box is small for what the child gets, which is what makes it work on a shelf where a 68 cm long dinosaur track set will not fit.

It sits at the bottom of this category at $5.49, above only the TF213415 storage dinosaur car at $4.38. That makes it the natural trial SKU for a buyer who wants to test the track category without committing to the moulded sets, and it also travels well: at 0.077 CBM per carton it is the cheapest model here to top up by the carton. The trade-off is that it carries no storage container, so the display story is the track itself rather than a vehicle that doubles as a box.
visible_features: Blue PVC track with two parallel lanes, supplied wound as a roll
Flexible strip that can be looped vertically, run flat or angled down
Black clamp stands with suction-cup feet to set the track height
Two small sports cars included in the box
Carton packed 16 pieces at 0.077 CBM, 1.25 kg per piece gross

TF216208.headline: The storage box is a dinosaur head
overview: The TF216208 is a 150-piece dinosaur track set packed inside a moulded dinosaur head. The head has an open mouth with a row of teeth and an amber eye, and it is the container as well as the pack: 29 cm wide, 20 cm deep and 19 cm high on its own, inside a printed box measuring 31.5 x 20.5 x 19.5 cm. The set builds a figure-of-eight layout roughly 68 x 28 cm with the track standing 7.5 cm deep, and the contents include green track segments, grey bridge sections, palm trees, several dinosaur species, yellow eggs and a three-car electric train with a green locomotive, a yellow wagon and a blue wagon.

That container is what the buyer is actually paying for, and the carton numbers show it. A carton holds 24 sets at 0.327 CBM, the largest cube per carton in this category, at 21 kg gross and 0.88 kg per set. A 20GP takes 85 cartons, 2,040 pieces. The 120-piece minimum is five cartons, 1.635 CBM. Because the head is hollow and the track nests inside it, the box is dense rather than bulky: 0.88 kg per set means the freight rate per unit stays reasonable even though the retail pack looks substantial.

Within the collection this is the mid-price dinosaur set. Below it the TF213415 at $4.38 is a storage dinosaur car with six pull-back cars and no track; above it the TF214357 at $7.57 is a 231-piece version whose container is a dinosaur-headed engineering truck. The TF216208 is the one where the container is the dinosaur itself, which is the version that reads as a gift box rather than as a playset with a storage feature.

Head measures 29 x 20 x 19 cm; printed box 31.5 x 20.5 x 19.5 cm

150 pieces, packed 24 sets per carton

TF214357.headline: 231 pieces, stored in an engineering truck
overview: The TF214357 is the larger of the two dinosaur track sets here, and the container this time is a dinosaur-headed engineering vehicle rather than a head on its own. A green dinosaur head forms the cab, and behind it a flatbed carries a moulded rail cage, so the truck reads as construction equipment when it is closed and as a storage tray when it is open. The 231 pieces build a wide oval with grey bridge sections, a red pavilion, palm trees, a volcano and a tunnel, and the contents include a multi-car electric train plus a spread of dinosaur figures and eggs.

Two numbers decide whether this goes by sea or air. A carton holds 18 sets at 0.246 CBM, 23.5 kg gross and 1.31 kg per set, which is heavier per unit than the TF216208 because of the truck body. A 20GP takes 113 cartons, 2,034 pieces. The 90-piece minimum is five cartons and 1.23 CBM, so the entry order is a small pallet-sized commitment rather than a container one.

Against the TF216208 at $6.42 the argument is pieces and container shape: 231 pieces against 150, and a vehicle rather than a head. Against the TF213426 at $13.38 the argument is the opposite. That model is a 12-car alloy set built around a launcher truck with no track at all, so it competes on the cars rather than on the layout. The TF214357 is the set you buy when the retail channel wants a big box with a lot inside it under ten dollars.

231 pieces, packed 18 sets per carton, 1.31 kg per set gross

TF213426.headline: A truck that swallows cars and launches them
overview: The TF213426 is built as a dinosaur-head truck with an open mouth at the front and a mechanism that feeds cars through it. Cars load at the rear on a fold-down ramp, sit inside the body, and are released out of the mouth, so the play pattern is load, store, launch rather than build and drive. The body carries an orange crane arm on top, a transparent side panel that shows how many cars are still inside, and moulded panels along the flank. Twelve alloy cars are included in the box, which is what separates this from every other item in this collection.

The weight is the thing to check before quoting air freight. A carton holds 20 sets at 0.22 CBM, 22 kg gross, giving 1.10 kg per set, and the alloy cars are the reason. A 20GP takes 127 cartons, 2,540 pieces, and the 100-piece minimum is five cartons and 1.1 CBM. By sea the density is fine; by air, twelve metal cars per unit is a cost you should price before you commit to a landed figure.

It only makes sense as the top of the dinosaur track range at $13.38, and it earns that by being a different product rather than a bigger version of the ones below. The TF214357 at $7.57 gives 231 pieces of track for the money; the TF213426 gives twelve die-cast cars, a launcher and a container, and no track. Retailers generally take one of each for that reason: they are not substitutes, and a display with both covers the child who wants to build and the child who wants to fire cars across a room.

Fold-down loading ramp at the rear and an internal carousel that feeds cars to the mouth

TF211091.headline: A vertical track the train falls through
overview: The TF211091 is a construction-style track rather than a moulded playmat. Interlocking track segments in blue, yellow and green slot together into towers and switchbacks, with white uprights holding the elevated sections, and the finished layout sends a white high-speed train down through a series of drops and turns instead of running it flat. Traffic signs, a bridge section and a small station piece are included. The set arrives packed flat in a 42 x 29.5 x 8.5 cm box, so what the customer carries home is a compact carton and what the child builds is roughly half a metre of vertical structure.

The packing is unusual for this catalogue and worth reading carefully. One carton holds only 6 sets, at 0.074 CBM and 32 kg gross, which comes to 5.33 kg per set, the heaviest per unit of any model here. The density is excellent, 378 cartons on a 20GP for 2,268 pieces, but the carton is heavy to handle and expensive to send by air. The 30-piece minimum is the lowest in the collection, five cartons at 0.37 CBM, which makes this the easiest model here to trial.

At $17.45 it is the second most expensive track model, behind the TF211082 at $20.54 for 121 pieces in a multicolour palette and ahead of the TF209512 at $10.80. The distinction between this and the TF211082 is the palette and the audience: the TF211091 is blue, yellow and green with a realistic train, which suits a transport-themed display; the TF211082 is bright multicolour with sports cars, which suits a general toy aisle. Both are construction sets, so a buyer usually takes one of the two rather than both.

TF211082.headline: The multicolour version, 121 pieces
overview: The TF211082 is the same construction idea as the TF211091 in a different palette: track segments in red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, slotted into vertical towers with white uprights, forming a looping elevated layout. Two vehicles are included, a red sports car and a silver car, and the box lists 121 pieces. The colour is the merchandising decision. Where the blue, yellow and green set reads as a railway, this one reads as a children's construction toy, which is why it is the version that sits in a general toy aisle rather than in a transport section.

Logistics are easier than the luxury version. A carton holds 12 sets at 0.126 CBM and 21.3 kg gross, 1.78 kg per set, so the carton is half the weight of the TF211091's and the cube per set is about the same. A 20GP takes 222 cartons, 2,664 pieces. The 60-piece minimum is five cartons and 0.63 CBM, still a trial-sized order, and the packing size of 23 x 19 x 19 cm is a small cube that displays well on a shelf edge.

At $20.54 it is the highest-priced track model in the collection, and the reason to take it over the $17.45 luxury version is the audience rather than the contents: more colour, cars instead of a train, 121 pieces against an unspecified count. A buyer who has room for only one construction track should choose by shelf: this one for a mixed toy aisle, the blue version for a transport or railway display.
